So as you can see selection sort works without any issue when it comes to the time and space complexity
of the selection sort.
In the worst case it's going to take on squared time complexity, because in this case we have two nested
loop inside each other.
So that's why selection sort always performs the same number of comparisons, regardless of whether
the array is sorted or not.
Now, when it comes to the space complexity, space complexity is O one because selection sort is an
in-place sorting algorithm, meaning it only uses constant amount of extra space, so the algorithm
does not require any additional storage proportional to the input size, aside from the new variables
using for comparison and swapping.
So that's why the space complexity is O one.
